summary: Checks whether a value is **not** a valid array-like length.
description: `nonLength(value)` is the same test as `!isLength(value)`, written so that a guard clause reads as a sentence rather than as a negation.
A whole number from `0` up to `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` — the range a `length` property may hold.
`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).
returns: `true` when the value is not a valid array-like length; otherwise `false`.

examples.title: What passes and what does not
examples.body:
```javascript
nonLength(-1); // => true
nonLength(1.5); // => true
nonLength("3"); // => true
nonLength(0); // => false
nonLength(42); // => false
nonLength(Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER); // => false
```
